title: Graphic Kahn–Kalai conjecture
statement_utf8:
There exists a constant $K>0$ such that, for any graph $H\subseteq K_n$, if $p\ge K p_E(H)\log v(H)$, then
$$
\Pr(G_{n,p}\text{ contains }H)\ge \frac12.
$$
Here the report defines the graphic expectation threshold by
$$
p_E(H):=\min\left\{p:\mathbb{E}[\#\text{ of }F\text{'s in }G_{n,p}]\ge 1\ \text{for every }F\subseteq H\right\}.
$$
classification_reason: Threshold pE and probability goal explicitly defined using standard random-graph copies.
quantifiers: There exists K>0 for all H subset Kn and p>=K pE(H) log v(H), containment probability>=1/2.
technical_disposition: HOLD_SOURCE_PRIOR: general expectation-threshold theorems are a strong prior objection requiring exact bridge to this pE; no novelty from an unverified bridge or isolated-vertex boundary.
source_followup: Report27/2024 printed1540-1541 selected Park contribution. Theorem6 involves q(F); Conjecture7 separately involves graphic pE(H). No bridge proved here, so the general theorem is not treated as a subsumer. No full successor proof read.
